guideTitle: The Best Rolling CPU Stands for Moving a PC Tower Easily
metaDescription: Rolling CPU stands let you pull a tower out for cleaning or cable changes. We compared eight on fit, locking casters, rails and extras like a built-in power outlet.
introParagraphs: A CPU stand with wheels does two jobs: it lifts the tower off the floor, which can help keep carpet fibers and dust away from the intakes, and it lets you roll the PC out to reach cables or clean behind it.

The details that separate them are fit (width and sometimes length adjustment), whether the casters lock so the stand doesn't drift, and side rails that keep the case from slipping. One pick here is a desk-height tower cart with a power outlet.
Most were under $35 at the time of writing. Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing; few listings state a weight capacity, so check before loading a heavy tower.

best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-1.summary: A low-cost, width-adjustable metal and PS stand with four casters, listed for floors and carpet.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-1.description:
This stand is the simple, low-cost rolling option: a metal and PS-plastic frame with adjustable width and four caster wheels, listed as suitable for hard floors and carpet.

The listing summary doesn't give dimensions, capacity or whether the casters lock.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-1.bestFor: Getting a standard tower rolling for little money.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-1.skipIf: You want locking wheels; the Hovadova adjustable stand has them.

best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-2.summary: Hovadova's adjustable stand with four 360-degree casters, locking wheels and tool-free setup.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-2.description:
The Hovadova adjustable stand adds locking wheels to the basics: four 360-degree casters, two of which lock, with tool-free setup. Hovadova says it lifts the tower away from dust, spills, carpet fibers and moisture.

It was under $17 at the time of writing. Dimensions aren't given in the listing summary.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-2.bestFor: Hard floors, where locking wheels stop drift.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-2.skipIf: You need side rails; the Hovadova Extra Large has them.

best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-3.summary: VIVO's low-profile steel mid-tower cart with four casters.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-3.description:
The VIVO is a low-profile steel cart for mid-tower cases, with four caster wheels. Steel construction and VIVO's established desk-accessory range are its main appeal.

The listing summary doesn't mention width adjustment or locking wheels, so check it fits your case.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-3.bestFor: A standard mid-tower that should sit low.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-3.skipIf: Your case is large; the Liitrton or AGPTEK adjusts length.

best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-4.summary: ZUAVIALA's height-adjustable tower cart (21.34 to 28.3 inches) with a built-in power outlet.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-4.description:
The ZUAVIALA is a different product: a tower cart whose top adjusts from 21.34 to 28.3 inches, so it can sit beside a desk as extra surface, with a built-in power outlet and a metal frame.

It was the most expensive option here at the time of writing and takes more floor space than a low stand.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-4.bestFor: Keeping a tower and power beside a desk that lacks space.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-4.skipIf: You just want the tower off the floor; a low stand costs a third as much.

best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-5.badge: Best Adjustable Length and Width for Less
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-5.summary: Liitrton's stand with adjustable length and width and four 360-degree casters.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-5.description:
The Liitrton adjusts both length (from 16.93 inches) and width to fit most towers, with four 360-degree casters, at under $15 at the time of writing.

That makes it the low-cost alternative to the AGPTEK for longer cases. Locking isn't mentioned in the listing summary.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-5.bestFor: Longer cases on a small budget.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-5.skipIf: You need a stated range; the AGPTEK lists 6.3–11.8 x 15.7–20 inches.

best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-6.summary: AGPTEK's stand adjusting 6.3 to 11.8 inches wide and 15.7 to 20 inches long.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-6.description:
The AGPTEK has the widest stated ranges here: 6.3 to 11.8 inches wide and 15.7 to 20 inches long, fitting slim cases through large towers, on four 360-degree casters.

It costs about twice the basic stands at the time of writing.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-6.skipIf: Your case is standard; the Hovadova adjustable is cheaper.

best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-7.summary: A width-adjustable stand that lifts the PC 1.75 inches, designed for carpet.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-7.description:
This stand raises the tower 1.75 inches off the floor, enough to clear carpet pile, with an adjustable width for most cases and free-rolling wheels.

The brand isn't named, and locking and capacity aren't stated in the listing summary.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-7.bestFor: Clearing carpet pile under a standard tower.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-7.skipIf: You want more clearance; the ZUAVIALA or taller stands lift higher.

best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-8.badge: Best for Large Cases with Rails
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-8.summary: Hovadova's extra-large rolling stand with side rails and four 360-degree wheels.
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-8.description:
The Hovadova Extra Large suits bigger towers, with protective rails on both sides to keep the case from slipping off and four 360-degree wheels.

It costs more than Hovadova's standard stand at the time of writing, and dimensions aren't given in the listing summary.
cons: Costs more than the standard Hovadova
best-cpu-stands-with-wheels-8.skipIf: Your case is mid-size; the standard Hovadova is cheaper.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Compare case width and depth with the stand's range; the AGPTEK lists the widest.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Prefer locking wheels on hard floors
buyingCriteria.explanation: They stop drift; the Hovadova adjustable lists them.
Rails help keep the case on the stand when rolling; the Hovadova Extra Large has them.
Most listings here don't state one; ask before loading a heavy tower.

faq.q: Why put a PC on wheels?
faq.a: To lift it off the floor and roll it out for cleaning or cable changes.
They help, especially on hard floors where a stand can drift.
Several are listed for carpet; larger casters roll more easily on thick pile.

faq.q: How much weight can they hold?
faq.a: Most listings here don't say; check before loading a heavy full tower.
It's a desk-height tower cart with an outlet, useful as a side surface beside the desk.

bottomLine: For a standard tower, the Hovadova adjustable stand adds locking wheels for very little, and the Liitrton or AGPTEK adjusts length for larger cases. The VIVO is a simple steel option.
For big cases, the Hovadova Extra Large adds rails, and the ZUAVIALA is the pick if you want a desk-height cart with power.
